overall: By my frame checks the 14B options are clearly best: big, readable motion (laughs, yawns, head turns), faces and outfits stay on model, and the train keeps its shape. They also take about 3.5 minutes per 5-second clip, faster than the 5B with a long prompt, because the 4-step speed-up does the work. Most of round 1's stiffness came from the prompts: the same 5B model moves a lot once the motion is written out per second. No clip here shows the rippling-skin train from round 1, but I only checked still frames and short frame pairs, so watch them in motion. Peak GPU is about 9.8 GB for everything because ComfyUI fills whatever the card has free and streams the rest from RAM; it is not a measure of what each model needs.
5b-plain: Too little motion. Mio is almost frozen; Rei only changes her smile.
5b-timed: Lots of motion and mostly on model. Slow (6 min portraits, 11 min for the scene). Some small drift in Mio's glasses.
14b-lx: Best balance. Follows the timed prompt closely, clean faces, rigid train cars.
14b-anime: Very close to plain 14B. The first few frames have a blotchy background and a small jump. No clear gain from the extra LoRAs.
dasiwa: As good as 14B plain on the portraits, and the only one that actually panned the camera on the monorail.
puppet-time: 4 blink inpaints (about 1 min of GPU each) plus drawn mouths; plays live
puppet: Fully consistent, since it is the approved sprite itself; loops forever; about 320 KB of images. It can't do big acting like a laugh or a head turn, which the 14B clips can.
puppet-how: Mio's approved RDBT sprite, cut into parts in code. The eyes swap between open, half and closed frames (the closed and half frames are face-only inpaints with RDBT, pasted back through a soft mask). The mouth frames are drawn to match her tiny line mouth, because the inpainted mouths came out as large glossy lips in a different style. A WebGL shader bends the loose strands and the bun around their roots, breathes (a slight stretch from the waist up) and tilts the head a little. Blinks come at random gaps of 2 to 6 seconds, sometimes twice. When a line plays, the loudness of her voice picks the mouth frame.
src-mio: Approved RDBT Mio (bored), 896×1152. The same sprite drives the puppet demo above.
src-monorail: The round-1 scene, 1280×704. The train faces the viewer, so the timed prompt sends it toward the lower left. The round-1 prompt sent it toward the city, against the way it faces.
rei-5b-plain: She smiles a little wider and her eyes narrow. Nothing else moves; no blink, no hair.
rei-5b-timed: Big change: she tilts her head, laughs with her eyes closed, turns away and back, and the ponytail follows. Face, hoops and suit stay on model. The motion is fast, close to twitchy in the middle.
rei-14b-lx: Closest to the prompt: blink, laugh with eyes closed, a head tilt, then a calm smile. Clean lines and a stable face. In the last frames a hand edges into the lower left corner.
rei-14b-anime: Same actions as plain 14B, including a wink. Faint noise in the background of the first frames.
rei-dasiwa: Blink, a wide open-mouth laugh with the head thrown back, then back to a smile. Crisp and on model; the most expressive of the Rei clips.
mio-5b-plain: Frozen: she barely changes over 2.4 s.
mio-5b-timed: A big yawn with her eyes shut, a head roll, then she opens her eyes and smiles. Good energy. Her glasses frame bends slightly in the last second.
mio-14b-lx: Yawn, eyes closed, a tired look back at the viewer, lips parted. Face and glasses hold up well. The sly smile at the end doesn't happen.
mio-14b-anime: Similar to plain 14B. The first frames have a blotchy background and a small jump before the motion starts.
mio-dasiwa: Softer yawn, eyes closed, head tilt; calmer than the others and stays on model.
monorail-5b-plain: The train moves toward the lower left and leaves the frame; the cars look rigid in the frames I checked. The camera creeps forward.
monorail-5b-timed: The train runs out of frame at the lower left and the last car passes, leaving an empty track, which makes physical sense. The cars keep their shape.
monorail-14b-lx: The train keeps coming at a steady speed; the cars stay rigid, and windows and doors stay in place. It never ends (cars keep appearing from the distance).
monorail-14b-anime: Almost the same as plain 14B: rigid cars, a steady speed, an endless train.
monorail-dasiwa: The camera pans left with the train, as asked; the city and sun slide across. Cars stay rigid. The most cinematic of the five.
